target: docs/41-试点关闭态旧课堂保护接线SDD.md
references: docs/36-全双工课堂统一提交接线设计.md §§15-18
summary: The fail-closed direction and closed-pilot boundary are appropriate, but security-critical contracts remain underspecified for writer ownership, unmigrated bridge serialization, authorization, cross-process deletion retirement, and old-binary deployment gating.

findings.title: Writer acquisition proof and tx-bound guard contract are unresolved
findings.risk: A deferred/read transaction or a guard result that survives rollback, commit, or pool changes could be mistaken for a serialized authorization check, allowing a legacy side effect after a competing mode change.
findings.required_revision: Freeze the exact SQLite writer-acquisition operation and transaction owner; use a transaction-bound capability that cannot outlive or cross its transaction/pool; recheck current scope under the writer; make all errors fail closed. Align with docs/36 §§15.3, 16, 17.

findings.title: Unmigrated legacy bridge and migration race behavior is implicit
findings.risk: Without the shared-writer bridge contract, a legacy reservation in a no-v2 database may not be visible to a concurrent migration/pilot creation, permitting incompatible mode facts across processes.
findings.required_revision: Specify bridge key/value and validation, writer acquisition/recheck order, atomic bridge insertion and COMMIT publication, migration import/retention, and fail-closed handling of malformed/unknown bridge data.

findings.title: Authorization principals and global/multi-scope authority are not frozen
findings.risk: A mode-fence receipt could be misused as authorization, or a global administrator/config operation could mutate all students' teaching state without an explicit per-scope authority contract.
findings.required_revision: Add a caller/principal matrix for direct service, tool, REST/WS, and workers; bind each requested student/book to current authorization; distinguish trusted system principals; enumerate global operation scopes before any effect and reject atomically if any scope is pilot, unknown, or unavailable.

findings.title: DeleteBook retirement does not define a durable cross-process callback fence
findings.risk: A process-local Room/task cancellation cannot prevent a different App process or late worker from recreating runtime state after cleanup, causing stale writes or data resurrection.
findings.required_revision: Define a persistent retirement generation/claim (or equivalent DB fence) checked by Enter/Join, workers, and every late callback; serialize deletion and in-flight effects; keep failed retirement closed for safe idempotent retry; freeze replay tombstone/retention before destructive cleanup.

findings.title: Old-binary exclusion is not an enforceable activation gate
findings.risk: A previously deployed writer can ignore persistent mode markers and write into a pilot scope after a newer version enables it.
findings.required_revision: Define a verifiable version/instance gate or stop-and-verify procedure before migration/pilot activation, and specify evidence required to unlock activation. If it cannot be enforced, keep migration and pilot permanently closed for that deployment.

findings.title: Unkeyed student scope hashes may be enumerable
findings.risk: Student identifiers drawn from a small domain can be recovered from an ordinary hash; raw book IDs may also reveal usage patterns.
findings.required_revision: Use access-controlled audit fields with retention limits, or keyed/rotating HMAC identifiers, and minimize raw scope identifiers in general logs.

findings.title: Commit-unknown resolution must require fresh durable proof
findings.risk: A pre-commit typed receipt or blind retry could cause callers to proceed without knowing whether the legacy reservation committed.
findings.required_revision: Resolve commit-unknown by rereading the exact scope/bridge under a fresh writer transaction; only observed durable matching state permits success. Otherwise return a fixed unknown/retryable error without allowing business effects.

limitations: This review evaluates design text and selected current boundary definitions only.
No code changes, tests, runtime experiments, deployment inventory, or authorization-path execution were performed.
A design review does not establish that current product paths are protected or that any pilot is ready.
